title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to specific requirements for the electric power train
scope_summary: Part I approves vehicle types of categories M, N and O (max design speed > 25 km/h) for the electrical safety of their electric power train and galvanically connected high voltage bus. Part II approves a Rechargeable Electrical Energy Storage System (REESS) type as a component/separate technical unit for M, N and O vehicles, and Part III approves the installation of an approved REESS on such vehicles; vehicles permanently connected to the grid are excluded throughout.
scope_quote: 1.1 Part I: Safety requirements with respect to the electric power train of road vehicles of categories M, N and O, with a maximum design speed exceeding 25 km/h, equipped with electric power train, excluding vehicles permanently connected to the grid. However, for vehicles of category O, with batteries which are charged by (one of) the vehicle's e-axle(s), the requirements in part I of this regulation shall apply, including those for the REESS (i.e. such batteries are considered as REESS even though they may not provide propulsion). ... 1.2 Part II: Safety requirements with respect to the Rechargeable Electrical Energy Storage System (REESS), of road vehicles of categories M, N and O equipped with electric power train, excluding vehicles permanently connected to the grid. Part II of this Regulation does not apply to a battery whose primary use is to supply power for starting the engine and/or lighting and/or other vehicle auxiliaries' systems. ... 1.3 Part III: Requirements with respect to the installation of an approved Rechargeable Electrical Energy Storage System (REESS) to the road vehicles of categories M, N and O equipped with electric power train, excluding vehicles permanently connected to the grid.
applies_to_components: Electric power train (traction motor(s), REESS, electric energy conversion system, electronic converters, associated wiring harness and connectors, coupling system for charging the REESS)
High voltage bus and galvanically connected high voltage components
Rechargeable Electrical Energy Storage System (REESS) and REESS subsystems
Batteries charged by e-axle(s) of category O vehicles
Electric energy conversion system (e.g. fuel cell)
Coupling system for charging the REESS
Exposed conductive parts / electrical chassis (potential equalization)
REESS protection functions: short circuit, overcharge, over-discharge, over-temperature, overcurrent protection
REESS thermal propagation and gas management
Prevention of accidental or unintended vehicle movement (active driving possible mode indication)
relation_to_other_regulations: Vehicle categories as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3), ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.6, para. 2
Flammable electrolyte defined by reference to UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods - Model Regulations (Rev. 17), Class 3 flammable liquid
Distinguishing numbers of Contracting Parties per Annex 3 of R.E.3
Approval marks may be combined with marks of other UN Regulations under which the vehicle/REESS is approved (para. 4.5)
Part I explicitly does not cover post-crash safety requirements (addressed elsewhere), HV components not galvanically connected to the HV bus, or HV connection between towing vehicle and trailer
Conformity of production per the 1958 Agreement procedures (Schedule 1, E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3)

defined_terms.label: Active driving possible mode
defined_terms.definition: Vehicle mode in which pressing the accelerator (or equivalent) or releasing the brake causes the electric power train to move the vehicle, or for category O, when coupled with a towing vehicle in that mode.

defined_terms.label: Aqueous electrolyte
defined_terms.definition: An electrolyte based on water solvent for the compounds providing conducting ions after dissociation.

defined_terms.label: Automatic disconnect
defined_terms.definition: A device that when triggered conductively separates the electric energy sources from the rest of the high voltage circuit of the electric power train.

defined_terms.label: Breakout harness
defined_terms.definition: Connector wires connected for testing purposes to the REESS on the traction side of the automatic disconnect.

defined_terms.label: Cell
defined_terms.definition: A single encased electrochemical unit with one positive and one negative terminal used as rechargeable electrical energy storage device.

defined_terms.label: Conductive connection
defined_terms.definition: Connection using connectors to an external power supply when the REESS is charged.

defined_terms.label: Connector
defined_terms.definition: Device providing mechanical connection and disconnection of high voltage electrical conductors to a mating component, including its housing.

defined_terms.label: Coupling system for charging the REESS
defined_terms.definition: The electrical circuit used for charging the REESS from an external electric power supply, including the vehicle inlet.

defined_terms.label: Electric energy conversion system
defined_terms.definition: A system (e.g. fuel cell) that generates and provides electric energy for electric propulsion.

defined_terms.label: Electric power train
defined_terms.definition: The electrical circuit including the traction motor(s) and possibly the REESS, electric energy conversion system, electronic converters, associated wiring harness and connectors, and the coupling system for charging the REESS.

defined_terms.label: Electrical chassis
defined_terms.definition: A set of conductive parts electrically linked together whose potential is taken as reference.

defined_terms.label: Electrical circuit
defined_terms.definition: An assembly of connected live parts designed to be electrically energized in normal operation.

defined_terms.label: Electrical protection barrier
defined_terms.definition: The part that provides protection against direct contact with high voltage live parts.

defined_terms.label: Electronic converter
defined_terms.definition: A device capable of controlling and/or converting electric power for electric propulsion.

defined_terms.label: Enclosure
defined_terms.definition: The part enclosing internal units and providing protection against any direct contact.

defined_terms.label: Exposed conductive part
defined_terms.definition: A conductive part touchable under IPXXB, not normally energized but which can become energized under isolation failure, including parts under covers removable without tools.

defined_terms.label: External electric power supply
defined_terms.definition: An AC or DC electric power supply outside of the vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Flammable electrolyte
defined_terms.definition: An electrolyte containing substances classified as Class 3 flammable liquid under the UN Model Regulations on Transport of Dangerous Goods.

defined_terms.label: High Voltage
defined_terms.definition: Classification of an electric component or circuit whose working voltage is > 60 V and ≤ 1500 V DC or > 30 V and ≤ 1000 V AC rms.

defined_terms.label: High voltage bus
defined_terms.definition: The electrical circuit, including the coupling system for charging the REESS, that operates on high voltage (only HV-operating parts where the specific voltage condition applies).

defined_terms.label: Live parts
defined_terms.definition: Conductive parts intended to be electrically energized under normal operating conditions.

defined_terms.label: Luggage compartment
defined_terms.definition: Space for luggage bounded by roof, hood, floor, side walls and HV protection barriers/enclosures, separated from the passenger compartment by a bulkhead.

defined_terms.label: On-board isolation resistance monitoring system
defined_terms.definition: Device which monitors the isolation resistance between the high voltage buses and the electrical chassis.

defined_terms.label: Open type traction battery
defined_terms.definition: A battery requiring filling with liquid and generating hydrogen gas released to the atmosphere.

defined_terms.label: Passenger compartment
defined_terms.definition: Space for occupant accommodation bounded by the body structure and by electrical protection barriers and enclosures protecting occupants from HV live parts.

defined_terms.label: Protection degree IPXXB
defined_terms.definition: Protection from contact with HV live parts by a barrier or enclosure, tested with the Jointed Test Finger per Annex 3.

defined_terms.label: Protection degree IPXXD
defined_terms.definition: Protection from contact with HV live parts by a barrier or enclosure, tested with the Test Wire per Annex 3.

defined_terms.label: Rechargeable Electrical Energy Storage System (REESS)
defined_terms.definition: Rechargeable energy storage system providing electric energy for propulsion, possibly including support, thermal management, electronic controls and casing, excluding batteries primarily for starting, lighting or auxiliaries.

defined_terms.label: REESS subsystem
defined_terms.definition: Any assembly of REESS components which stores energy, with or without the entire REESS management system.

defined_terms.label: Service disconnect
defined_terms.definition: Device for deactivation of the electrical circuit when conducting checks and services of the REESS, fuel cell stack, etc.

defined_terms.label: Solid insulator
defined_terms.definition: Insulating coating of wiring harnesses covering HV live parts to prevent direct contact.

defined_terms.label: Specific voltage condition
defined_terms.definition: Condition where the maximum voltage of a galvanically connected circuit between a DC live part and any other live part is ≤ 30 V AC rms and ≤ 60 V DC.

defined_terms.label: Tested-Device
defined_terms.definition: Either the complete REESS or a REESS subsystem subjected to the tests of this Regulation.

defined_terms.label: Thermal event
defined_terms.definition: Condition when the temperature within the REESS is significantly higher (as defined by the manufacturer) than the maximum operating temperature.

defined_terms.label: Thermal runaway
defined_terms.definition: Uncontrolled increase of cell temperature caused by exothermic reactions inside the cell.

defined_terms.label: Thermal propagation
defined_terms.definition: Sequential occurrence of thermal runaway within a REESS triggered by thermal runaway of a cell in that REESS.

defined_terms.label: Type of REESS
defined_terms.definition: Systems not differing significantly in trade name, cell chemistry/capacity/dimensions, number and connection/support of cells, casing construction/materials, and ancillary devices for support, thermal management and electronic control.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle connector
defined_terms.definition: Device inserted into the vehicle inlet to supply electric energy from an external electric power supply.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle inlet
defined_terms.definition: Device on the externally chargeable vehicle into which the vehicle connector is inserted to transfer electric energy.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle type
defined_terms.definition: Vehicles not differing in installation, nature and type of the electric power train and the galvanically connected high voltage bus/components.

defined_terms.label: Venting
defined_terms.definition: Release of excessive internal pressure from a cell, REESS subsystem or REESS in a manner intended by design to preclude rupture or explosion.

defined_terms.label: Working voltage
defined_terms.definition: Highest rms circuit voltage specified by the manufacturer that may occur between conductive parts in open circuit or normal operation, defined per galvanically isolated circuit.

defined_terms.label: Trailer load compartment
defined_terms.definition: Compartment of the trailer described by the bodywork, including the loading floor, inner bodywork surfaces and storage equipment.

defined_terms.label: e-axle
defined_terms.definition: An axle mounted to a category O vehicle generating electrical energy and/or providing electrical propulsion.

defined_terms.label: Alkali metal anodes
defined_terms.definition: Negative electrodes of battery cells based on lithium, sodium or potassium, e.g. alkali metal foils or alkali metals encapsulated in host structures.

applicability_hints: Any traction battery of a battery-electric, hybrid or fuel cell vehicle is a REESS and can be approved separately under Part II (mark '…R-ES') or assessed within the vehicle approval.
Batteries of trailers (category O) charged by an e-axle are treated as REESS even if they do not provide propulsion.
12 V/24 V starting, lighting or auxiliary batteries are excluded from the REESS definition and Part II.

Any HV component galvanically connected to the HV bus (e.g. on-board charger, DC/DC converter, inverter, electric A/C compressor, HV heater, HV cables and connectors, charging inlet) is covered by Part I electric shock protection requirements, whether or not it contributes to propulsion.
HV components/systems galvanically isolated from the traction HV bus are outside Part I.
Circuits meeting the specific voltage condition (≤ 60 V DC, ≤ 30 V AC rms) are not HV, e.g. 48 V mild-hybrid systems generally fall below the HV threshold for shock protection.
The vehicle inlet and charging coupling system are part of the high voltage bus, so charging inlets fall under Part I.
Fuel cell stacks are covered as an electric energy conversion system within the electric power train.
Part I applies only to vehicles with max design speed > 25 km/h; Part II and III have no speed limit stated.
Vehicles permanently connected to the grid (e.g. trolleybuses on catenary) are excluded.
HV connections between towing vehicle and trailer and post-crash safety are not covered by Part I.
Battery management, thermal management, casing and support structures are part of the REESS and therefore within the REESS type and its tests.
REESS subsystems (modules) may be used as Tested-Devices for many Part II tests.
Open type traction batteries (aqueous electrolyte releasing hydrogen) trigger hydrogen emission requirements (5.4, Annex 8).
Cells with alkali metal anodes (lithium-metal, sodium, potassium) are specifically defined and may attract specific requirements.
Enclosures, covers, protection barriers, insulation of HV wiring and potential-equalization bonding parts are relevant to Part I even if they are passive mechanical parts.
Vehicle control functions (ready/active driving possible mode indication, drive-away prevention while conductively connected to charger) are within Part I.
